bug.title: ProcessEvaluator workers outlive a killed campaign driver and keep starting sandboxes
bug.symptoms: After the campaign driver is killed, its spawn workers continue evaluating queued nodes, which start runsc sandboxes, until they are killed by hand.
bug.reproduction_steps: Start a ProcessEvaluator with 2 workers from a child process. Submit evaluations that each run for several seconds. SIGKILL the child (the driver). Its workers stay alive and keep running.
bug.expected: - _init_worker records the parent's pid when the worker starts, and starts a daemon watchdog thread. Every 2 seconds the thread checks whether the parent is gone: os.getppid() no longer equals the recorded pid, or the parent's pid is not alive. If it is gone, the worker ends at once with os._exit(..), with a nonzero code named in a constant. This holds even mid-evaluation, so a sandbox subprocess in progress is orphaned no further than the existing timeout allows. On Linux the worker also sets PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (SIGTERM) through prctl via ctypes. If that call is unavailable, it is skipped, and the watchdog is the portable guarantee. - Normal shutdown (the executor's shutdown) is unchanged. A worker whose parent is alive is never stopped by the watchdog. - test_process_pool_orphan_exit.py covers: - the reproduction: a driver subprocess is SIGKILLed while its workers run a sleep task, and every worker pid has gone within 10 seconds - a live parent: the workers survive 5 seconds of idle time It uses only a stub task (no sandbox and no snapshot) and passes under pytest-xdist. The orchestrator member suite passes (run at -n 2).
bug.actual: Root cause: spawn workers have no link to the driver's lifetime. The executor cleans them up only through an orderly shutdown, which a signal or SIGKILL never runs.
bug.constraints: Only the two listed files change Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
